messages.subject: Subjunc running time
messages.body_plain:
Hi all.

I'm running subjunc on a set of RNA-seq datasets from patients with (probably) DSB-repair-derived chromosomal aberrations (HiSeq with TruSeq chemistry, blood samples, no depletion). The idea is to characterize the transcriptome of each one, specially the indels. So my questions is: how do subjunc running time scale with respect to the -I parameter? And what is the effect of the --complexIndels option?

I've tested two runs with these commands:

subjunc -T54 -i ../../genomes/UCSC/hg38/Rsubread/hg38.fa.masked.idx -r Karina_CAGATC_L004.fastq.gz -o Karina_CAGATC_L004_I17.bam.aln  --allJunctions -u --rg-id "RG" > Karina_CAGATC_L004_I17.log 2> Karina_CAGATC_L004_I17.err &

subjunc -T54 -i ../../genomes/UCSC/hg38/Rsubread/hg38.fa.masked.idx -r Karina_CAGATC_L004.fastq.gz -o Karina_CAGATC_L004_I17.bam.aln  --allJunctions -I17 -u --rg-id "RG" > Karina_CAGATC_L004_I17.log 2> Karina_CAGATC_L004_I17.err &

The first run took 163.7 minutes and the second (with -I17) 588.3 minutes. I was unable to finish the run with --complexIndels.

Secondly, subjunc doesn't seems to take full advantage of threads/cores. Why? I wasn't able to use more than 40 threads at a time (my server has 64 cores).

That's it for now. Logs attached.

Thanks in advance,

Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Subjunc running time
messages.body_plain:
Dear Daniel,

When the value provided to '-I' option is greater than 16, subjunc (and also subread aligner) will perform read assembly to try to discover long indels and this will increase the running time of the program.

Turning on '--complexIndels' option could significantly increase the running time if the error rate in your data is high. So the running time associated with this option is data specific. Subjunc/subread firstly builds a global indel table and then re-align all the reads by taking into account indels in the table. A high error rate in the input data could result in the creation of a large indel table and the realignment step will take much longer.

Subjunc/subread has a hard coded limit on the number of threads used by the program for mapping and this limit is 40 threads. We can change this limit and I do not feel the running time will be improved much by using more threads than that because of the I/O cost from each thread.

Best wishes,

Wei
